channel.title: Arabic — Planet Leads Academy
channel.description: Arabic words are given in Arabic script with a transliteration; transliteration is approximate, and listening to native speakers is the best check. This course teaches Modern Standard Arabic, the written and formal spoken variety used across the Arab world, while noting where everyday speech differs.

item.title: Greetings, Introductions, and Politeness
item.description: Lesson 2: Greetings, Introductions, and Politeness Arabic greetings carry warmth and a religious and cultural history, and using them correctly is one of the fastest ways to be welcomed in conversation. The most universal greeting is السلام عليكم (as-salaamu ʿalaykum, "Peace be upon you"). The…

item.title: Nouns, Gender, and the Definite Article
item.description: Lesson 3: Nouns, Gender, and the Definite Article Arabic nouns have two genders, masculine and feminine, and gender affects adjectives, pronouns, and verb forms. There is no neuter gender. Most nouns are masculine by default; feminine nouns are often marked by the ending ة (taa marbuuṭa)…

item.title: Pronouns and Present-Tense Verbs
item.description: Lesson 4: Pronouns and Present-Tense Verbs Arabic pronouns distinguish gender and number, including the dual. The independent pronouns are: أنا (anaa, "I"), أنتَ (anta, "you", to a man), أنتِ (anti, "you", to a woman), هو (huwa, "he"), هي (hiya, "she"), نحن (naḥnu, "we"), أنتم (antum, "you"…

item.title: Adjectives, Possession, and Description
item.description: Lesson 5: Adjectives, Possession, and Description Arabic adjectives agree with the noun they describe in gender, number, and definiteness, and they normally follow the noun, the opposite order from English. A new book is كتاب جديد (kitaab jadiid, literally "book new"), a new school is مدرسة جديدة…

item.title: Past Tense and the Verb System
item.description: Lesson 6: Past Tense and the Verb System Arabic past tense is formed with suffixes attached to the past stem, and it is in some ways more regular than the present tense, because there are no prefixes to learn — only suffixes. For the verb كتب (kataba, "he wrote"), the past conjugation is: أنا كتبتُ…

item.title: Numbers, Time, and Days
item.description: Lesson 7: Numbers, Time, and Days Arabic numbers 1 to 10 are: واحد (waaḥid, 1), اثنان (ithnaan, 2), ثلاثة (thalaatha, 3), أربعة (arbaʿa, 4), خمسة (khamsa, 5), ستة (sitta, 6), سبعة (sabʿa, 7), ثمانية (thamaaniya, 8), تسعة (tisʿa, 9), عشرة (ʿashara, 10).
